questions.question: Explain the basic economic problem and state the three basic economic questions.
questions.expected_answer: Human wants are unlimited, but the resources (factors of production) available to satisfy them are scarce, so choices must be made, each with an opportunity cost. The three questions are: what to produce, how to produce it, and for whom to produce.

questions.question: Compare the planned and market economies in terms of ownership of resources, who makes decisions, and how prices are set, and name the thinker linked to each.
questions.expected_answer: Planned: the state owns most factors of production; a central planning authority decides what, how and for whom; prices are set by the state; linked to Karl Marx (The Communist Manifesto, 1848). Market: factors are privately owned; consumers and businesses decide through markets; prices are set by demand and supply (the price mechanism); linked to Adam Smith (The Wealth of Nations, 1776).

questions.question: Give three pieces of evidence that South Africa has a mixed economy.
questions.expected_answer: Any three, for example: most businesses are privately owned and prices are set by demand and supply; the state owns enterprises such as Eskom and Transnet; the state provides public goods and services such as schools, clinics, police and social grants funded by taxes; the state regulates markets, e.g. the minimum wage and the Competition Commission.
